publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.7 redacts recognizable API keys before heartbeat (scheduled job) output is stored: keys of well-known shapes such as sk_live_, rk_live_ and pk_test_ payment keys, GitHub tokens, AWS access keys, sk- keys, JSON web tokens and private-key blocks become [redacted] before the failure excerpt is saved, on top of the phrases you list under Output text to mask and the labelled secrets that were already masked; output stored by 0.5.6 or earlier is not rewritten, so rotate a key that earlier output may have contained, and a secret with no recognizable shape can still be stored. Period reports now open in their own wide view from Generate report on the monitor's Reports section, with a Back to monitor link, the period and filters under Change period or filters, and durations in plain words. The scheduled-job screen puts its reporting commands behind Job reporting instructions and shows each receipt as Started, Finished successfully or Failed in your own time, with before your last edit on receipts that came earlier. Sent alerts and test sends that were only simulated (development email or the demo) read Simulated · no email sent, alerts restored from an archive read Imported, sending held, and delivery states read plainly: scheduled-drill history, schedule state and fallback reasons use words such as Destination disabled, Credentials changed, Confirmed by recipient, Active and delivery timed out instead of internal codes. No migration and no new required settings; the pinned @runeditrun/rer stays at 0.2.108; update an existing checkout with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Known issues: a monitor CSV exported from UptimeRobot still cannot be imported (the v3 JSON, an event-log CSV and Uptime's own url CSV are read); restoring an installation archive does not bring back the list of erased people, so a Business that pairs again after a restore and still lists an erased person could invite them again; a company that has signed an agent policy but never sent company settings is treated as running, so its feed answers with an empty page (no token or decision is shared); a response body over 64 KiB still fails the check, so monitor a smaller page such as a health endpoint. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0, 0.5.1, 0.5.2, 0.5.3, 0.5.4, 0.5.5, 0.5.6 and 0.5.7.
